newsitem.title: JAPAN: Venezuela seeks renegotiation of CVG's Japan debt.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela seeks renegotiation of CVG's Japan debt.

text.p: A delegation of Venezuelan officials proposed a renegotiation of state-owned Corporacion Venezolana de Guyana's (CVG) debts with Japanese banks during a meeting Monday with directors of the Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi Ltd, the delegation said in a statement.
The government hopes to privatize CVG, which includes large aluminium and steel operations, in the months ahead.

"The proposal of CVG to Japanese banking institutions is to utilize resources obtained from the privatization of Venezuelan aluminium and steel in order to reduce the debt and get better terms for the remaining amounts," the statement said.

The statement did not indicate the levels of debt involved or give further details of the proposal and no officials were available for comment. CVG president Elias Ynaty said in July that CVG's aluminium sector has $1.2 billion in debt.

The delegation, which includes Ynaty and Venezuelan Investment Fund (FIV) president Alberto Poletto, will hold key talks on Tuesday and Wednesday with a Japanese consortium, led by Showa Denko KK, that owns 20 percent of the 430,000 tonne-per-year capacity Venalum refinery, the crown jewel of CVG's aluminium holdings.

The Venezuelans and Japanese have been locked in a dispute since the beginning of the year regarding the Japanese group's veto power over Venalum decisions, which Venezuelan officials argue will reduce the price paid for the enterprise when the bulk of the government's 80 percent stake is privatised.
